groundTruthNarrative: The region's genuine pipeline barely moved in Q3: rep-created open pipeline went from $8.1M to $8.4M. Win rates (23–25%) and cycle times (71–74 days) on genuine opportunities held steady, so flat bookings are what that flat genuine pipeline would produce. The reported jump to $14.6M comes almost entirely from 212 records worth $6.2M, loaded by Data Import late on 29 Sept, the night before the coverage snapshot that gates Q4 hiring. They were loaded under the sales operations analyst's account from a spreadsheet tagged as Brightwell partner referrals. Brightwell registered only three deals worth $0.21M in the period and sent no bulk list. 171 of the 212 records clone 2024 closed-lost opportunities with the close dates moved forward. None has any logged activity, and nearly half the contacts are stale. Owners were assigned from the file, so reps did not create the records, and their 'conversion' figures were dragged down by records they never worked. The webinar series produced only $0.46M of opportunities; its $5.9M 'influenced' figure is an attribution artefact that counts the imported records. Okafor's own authenticated session ran the import. Who prepared and posted the file is unestablished: the chat messages were auto-deleted, several channel members had the same coverage incentive, and Wexley's ambiguous 28 Sept instruction is temporally associated with the import but not shown to have caused it. The retained source file is the next evidence to examine.

answers.rationale: C1 shows that 212 import-created records worth $6.2M, with no activity and 171 cloned from 2024 closed-lost deals, make up almost all of the $6.5M growth in E1. C3 confirms that rep-created pipeline rose only $0.3M. C2 and C9 corroborate that the records are not genuine.

The 13% conversion figure in E1/E2 is computed on an inflated denominator. C3 shows win rates of 24%, 23% and 25% and steady cycle times on rep-created opportunities. The four named reps sit at 21–26%, within the regional range.

C4 shows the series created only 11 opportunities worth $0.46M. The $5.9M 'influenced' figure counts $4.1M of import-created records and $1.34M of opportunities opened before the series began. E5 also places the surge after the series ended.

E2 shows Wexley pressed for partner deals before the snapshot, and C1 shows the import ran the next night from a file of unknown authorship. Several channel members shared the coverage incentive (E4). The messages are deleted (C5), and her denial is interested (C6). Nothing available identifies the file's author, so the claim is live but unestablished.

C1 shows the inflating records came from a single data import under a sales operations account, with owners set from the file. Rep-created additions in the same window were normal ($0.70M). C3 shows rep-created pipeline essentially flat. E6 and C10 report that reps did not create or recognise the records.

Reported pipeline is the sum of open records. C1 shows the 212 records ($6.2M) entered the pipeline on 29 Sept, before the snapshot. With them excluded, pipeline is $8.4M against $8.1M (C3). The mechanism, the timing and the arithmetic decomposition establish the link.
The webinar sourced $0.46M of a $6.5M increase (C4). The surge came after the series ended and consists of records sourced as Brightwell imports (E5, C1).

The instruction (28 Sept, E2) came the day before the import (29 Sept, C1), and both concern partner deals before the snapshot, so they co-occur. The instruction asked for 'real' deals, though. The person who prepared the file is unknown, and others had the same snapshot motive independently (E4), so causation is not established.
Closing effectiveness did not decline (C3). Bookings are flat because genuine pipeline is flat, not because reps are converting worse.

Whoever authored the file, the records are shown not to reflect genuine demand (C1, C2, C9). Restating coverage at about 1.9x ($8.4M/$4.4M from C3) protects the hiring gate and removes the distortion from rep metrics.
The four reps' low ratios result from being assigned 129 of the imported records (C3). Their genuine win rates are normal. Putting them on performance plans punishes the wrong people.
This would be justified only if H4 were confirmed, and H4 is unknown. The retained source file and the investigation in A4 could settle it.

C1 notes that the source file is retained but unexamined. Its metadata and the surrounding records are the most direct route to resolving who fabricated the records, which any personnel decision depends on.

The 3.3x coverage rests on the gamed records. Genuine coverage is about 1.9x, below the 3.0x gate in E4. Releasing the requisitions on this basis rewards the fabrication and defeats the hiring control.

The evidence is sufficient for substantive steps: quarantining the records, restating coverage, and refusing both the performance plans and the release of requisitions on the reported figure. Only the attribution of individual culpability remains open, and none of these steps depends on it.

authoringNotes: Initial-file traps: the director's closing narrative and the 13% conversion figure (E1/E2), marketing's $5.9M influenced figure (E3), and an apparent rep-originated surge. Hints that keep the case fair: the one-week $6.9M spike after the webinar ended (E5), the coverage gate (E4), and Reyna not recognising partner deals assigned to him (E6). The provenance clue is in C1: the import job, the operations account, owners set from the file, clones of 2024 closed-lost deals, and zero activity. C2 and C9 corroborate it independently. Who authored the file is deliberately unresolvable: the chat messages auto-deleted, six channel members share the scorecard incentive, Wexley's 'real partner deal' wording is ambiguous, and C12 shows only that Okafor himself ran the import. That keeps H4 unknown, R3 association-only and A3 premature, while A4 points to the retained file. C5, C6, C10 and C12 bear on the case but change no expected answer. They are omitted from both read lists. Dates were checked: 28 Sept 2026 is a Monday and the 30 Sept snapshot falls on a Wednesday. Numbers reconcile: 8.4 + 6.2 = 14.6; 6.2 + 0.7 = 6.9; 4.1 + 1.34 + 0.46 = 5.9; 236 − 59 = 177.
